pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: features/dukazy/dukazySource.test.ts:11 This blocking source-grep guard checks that the loader uses the bill-id codec by matching the raw file text (readFileSync with no comment stripping). A comment quoting the import line would pass it even if the codec were never used, which is the 'prose satisfies the matcher' failure; the sibling a11y.test.ts in the same folder does strip comments first.

techniques.evidence: features/dukazy/dukazySource.test.ts:6 The presence and absence assertions run over raw text, with no normalisation to executable code and no note saying that over-detection is the safe direction. Contrast a11y.test.ts:16 stripComments, though that is a regex pass with no seeded pair of fixtures.
features/dukazy/messages.test.ts:92 The earlier catalog gate skipped plural keys, which shrank its population. It now gates every key, removing the scoped-population false green.
features/dukazy/messages.test.ts:60 A measured false positive (column identifiers scored as English) was fixed in the detector, by stripping identifiers, and the gate was kept.

pairs.evidence: features/schranka/telemetryScrub.test.ts:138 The guard that the privacy scrub is wired into both Sentry configs matches raw file text, so a commented-out `// beforeSend: scrubFollowTelemetry` would keep it green while follow keys leak. This is exactly the measured comment-satisfies-binding failure the technique describes.

techniques.evidence: features/schranka/telemetryScrub.test.ts:132 There is no comment or string stripping before the binding assertions. schrankaSource.test.ts:7 has the same raw-read pattern for its import-presence checks (line 12).
features/schranka/messages.test.ts:12 The catalog pin states the question it does NOT answer (ICU placeholder parity), so its green is not read as covering that.
